info.title: TrueBiz Web Presence Review API
info.description:
# Introduction
TrueBiz provides tools to automate assessing a merchant's web presence through the entire customer lifecycle.

# Authentication

All requests to TrueBiz require an API key to be sent as a header.  The expected header name is "X-API-KEY".

post.description:
Conduct a web presence review of a business. You must identify the business one of two ways:

- **By domain** — submit `domain` (accepts a bare domain, full URL, or email; we extract the registered
   domain).
- **By name + address** — submit `submitted_business_name` together with at least one address field
   (`address_line_1`, `city`, `state_province`, `postal_code`, or `country`).

All other fields (`submitted_phone`, `submitted_email`, `submitted_full_name`, `submitted_description`)
are optional and help us identify the business and surface additional detail.

Requires a valid `X-API-KEY` header. Rate limited to 5 requests per second.

**Testing:** You can use `example.org` as a test domain to verify your integration without
hitting real data sources or incurring any cost to you. It returns a static fixture response with realistic data.

This API endpoint allows you to enqueue a web presence review based on either a website (as a URL, domain,
or email) or both a business name and address. Other optional information about the company and
 applicant (phone, email, applicant name) can help identify the business and locate additional detail.
You may either poll for status updates using the url provided in the response's `Location` header, or,
if you have a webhook configured, wait for us to notify you when the web presence review is completed.
(You may then request the details from the Web Presence Review History endpoint.)
This API requires a valid API key (X-API-KEY) to be  provided in the headers and is rate limited to 5 requests
per second.

Create Industry Search endpoints allow you to start a new industry discovery request. You provide a business
name and location details, and TrueBiz creates a search record. The response includes a unique identifier for
the search, which can be used to retrieve the results from the corresponding retrieval endpoint once processing
is complete. In addition to the the ID returned in the response body, the full retrieval URL is also included
in the Location header sent with the response.

This API requires a valid API key (X-API-KEY) to be provided in the headers and is rate limited to 5
requests per second.

get.description:
The List Industry Searches endpoint retrieves a list of all industry discovery requests associated with the
account linked to the provided API key. Each entry in the list includes the unique identifier, creation and
update timestamps, current status, and a brief status description. If a search has been completed, the
result field will contain the discovered industry information; otherwise, it will be null.

The Get Industry Search endpoint retrieves the status and results of a previously created industry discovery
request. If the discovery is still in progress, the endpoint responds with HTTP 202 (Accepted). When the discovery
is complete, the endpoint responds with HTTP 200 (OK) and returns the discovered industry information,
including name, address, description, and industry classifications (e.g., NAICS, SIC, MCC).

Clients should poll the Get Industry Search endpoint using exponential backoff rather than continuous requests.
We recommend starting with a short delay (2–3 seconds) after the initial 202 response, then doubling the wait
time between each subsequent attempt until reaching a maximum interval (for example, 30 seconds). Continue polling
until the endpoint returns 200 (discovery complete) or until a reasonable overall timeout is reached. This
approach reduces unnecessary load while ensuring timely retrieval of results.

This API requires a valid API key (X-API-KEY) to be provided in the headers and is rate limited to 5
requests per second.

tags.description:
# Business Purpose

Users of TrueBiz's Web Presence Review API want to be able to submit a request and have it respond with a completed
Web Presence Review within 30 seconds.

# Technical Overview

Our synchronous web presence review API's allow you to submit information about a business website needing a review.
The minimum needed to identify a business is one of:
- a website (as a URL, domain, or email address)
- a business name and address
Additional information about the business and applicant (phone, email, or name) can be optionally submitted to improve results.
The API will respond to the HTTP request containing the expected responses as documented
elsewhere. See our OpenAPI spec for the exact schema details.

# Implementation details

## API Key

To submit a request to TrueBiz, you will also need an API Key. If you do not already have one, contact your account
manager.

## Risk Profile

If you want to override TrueBiz's default risk settings, you can do so within our Web Portal.  Click the Settings
button at the top, then "Create Profile". Go through the steps, and then your account manager will contact you with
any additional follow up questions and when complete, your risk profile id.

## Sending the request for a Web Presence Review

Sending a request to TrueBiz's synchronous URL, Email, or Review Company endpoints is simple, it requires a one time HTTP request.
Note that you'll need to provide a valid, non-example API Key. If you are using a risk profile, you'll need to provide
a valid ID for that. If you are not, simply remove the parameter or set it to a null value. Here's some example code
in python, assuming your API key is "446de5ee-198e-4a29-9cd3-190252866961" and your match (risk) profile id
is "4a0e18d9-b2d7-4fac-9f31-854ff5da92b4":

```
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "446de5ee-198e-4a29-9cd3-190252866961"}
response = httpx.post(
    "http://localhost:8600/api/v1/company/search",
    json={
      "domain": "https://truebiz.io/",
      "submitted_business_name": "Truebiz",
      "address_line_1": "123 Main St.",
      "address_line_2": "Suite 100",
      "city": "Memphis",
      "state_province": "TN",
      "postal_code": "37501",
      "country": "USA",
      "submitted_email": "bob@yahoo.com",
      "submitted_phone": "(901) 555-5555",
      "submitted_full_name": "Bob Smith",
      "match_profile_id": "4a0e18d9-b2d7-4fac-9f31-854ff5da92b4"
    },
    headers=headers,
)
```

The HTTP status code should indicate if the request completed successfully or not. If it did, the full web
presence review will be packaged into the json and if not, error details should be provided. See our OpenAPI
spec for the exact schema details.

manager.

button at the top, then "Create Profile". Go through the steps, and then your account manager will contact you with
any additional follow up questions and when complete, your risk profile id.

```
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "446de5ee-198e-4a29-9cd3-190252866961"}
response = httpx.post(
    "http://localhost:8600/api/v1/company/async/search",
    json={
      "domain": "https://truebiz.io/",
      "submitted_business_name": "Truebiz",
      "address_line_1": "123 Main St.",
      "address_line_2": "Suite 100",
      "city": "Memphis",
      "state_province": "TN",
      "postal_code": "37501",
      "country": "USA",

      "match_profile_id": "4a0e18d9-b2d7-4fac-9f31-854ff5da92b4"
    },
    headers=headers,
)
```

The response will contain important information:
  * HTTP Status Code: A 200 status code indicates that everything processed well. Other status codes are used as appropriate for error conditions.
  * Message: A human readable message indicating whether the message was successfully submitted for processing.
  * Tracking ID: The ID for this review as it is known to TrueBiz.

See our OpenAPI spec for the exact schema details.

## Waiting for the Webhook Notification and Getting the Response

Once the web presence review is complete, you should receive a webhook notification indicating processing has completed.
For security purposes, this message contains limited information:
  * Message ("message": str): A human readable message indicating whether the web presence review completed successfully or not.
  * Tracking ID ("tracking_id": UUID4): The ID for this review as it is known to TrueBiz.

From there, you can submit a request to TrueBiz's Web Presence Review History endpoint to get the results. Example
code in python, assuming that your API key is "446de5ee-198e-4a29-9cd3-190252866961" and the tracking ID is
"e968dac7-f829-4183-9e29-6da68868484a":

```

tracking_id = "e968dac7-f829-4183-9e29-6da68868484a"

```

tags.name: Auth Relay Guide
tags.description:
# Business Purpose

Users of TrueBiz that maintain customer relationship management (CRM) systems want to be able to expose our results in their CRM.  As TrueBiz exposes a large amount of data, this can be cumbersome and delay the integration process.  To speed up integration of TrueBiz's Web Presence Review, many customers want to be able to link directly from their CRM to TrueBiz's existing web portal.  To speed up that linkage, TrueBiz offers a read-only view of our Web Presence Review based on the IETF Digital Signatures Draft Standards.

# Technical Overview

The IETF Digital Signatures Draft proposal allows TrueBiz to authenticate that a request came from our customer to view components in our UI through the use of a shared secret and a known URL composition structure.  Prior to implementation, TrueBiz will provide our customer with a known public identifier (a UUID4 string) and a secret value (a different UUID4 string).  When the customer requests a company search, we will respond with the appropriate results and include a tracking_id (UUID4 string). This is combined with a few query parameters (including a timestamp indicating how long the signature is valid for) to produce a unique URL.  With the known shared secret and full url, a signature is generated using SHA256-HMAC and this is added as a query parameter.  This link is sent to TrueBiz, who uses our knowledge of the shared secret to create a hash and compare that it matches the signature provided.  If the signature matches, we allow the request to proceed.  If it does not, we provide a generic authentication error.

# Implementation Details

Prior to implementing any code, TrueBiz will provide our customer with a public ID (a UUID4 string) and a secret value (a different UUID4 string).  We will provide our relay auth endpoint as well - https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/relay/auth/{request_id}.  You will fill out the request_id parameter using the tracking_id field from a web presence review that has already been completed. To send a request to Truebiz, you must also include the following query parameters IN THIS SPECIFIC ORDER:
* version: The version of this implementation you are using.  Currently, the only valid value is 1.  It is expected this value will always be a positive integer greater or equal to 1
* valid_until: The time this redirect link should be valid until. Note that this is expected to be in epoch-time format, and thus is expected to be an integer.  The value must fall between -5 and 300 seconds of the current time on TrueBiz's API servers.
* public_id: The public identifier for the shared secret - a UUID4 string.
* signature: The HMAC-SHA256 value generated using the shared secret and the URL with all query parameters except the signature.  It is expected this will always be a UUID4 string.

Example code (python):
```python
from base64 import urlsafe_b64encode
import datetime
import hashlib
import hmac
import pytz
from typing import Optional
import uuid
import urllib.parse

from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta


def generate_url_with_digital_signature(
        *,
        request_id: uuid.UUID,
        valid_until: Optional[datetime.datetime],
        public_id: uuid.UUID,
        secret_value: uuid.UUID,
        version: int = 1,
) -> str:
    base_url = f"https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/relay/auth/{request_id}"
    query_parameters = {
        "valid_until": valid_until.strftime("%s")
        if valid_until
        else str((datetime.datetime.utcnow().replace(tzinfo=pytz.utc) + relativedelta(seconds=60)).strftime("%s")),
        "version": f"{version}",
        "public_id": str(public_id),
    }
    computed_url = f"{base_url}?{urllib.parse.urlencode(query_parameters)}"
    signature = hmac.new(bytes(str(secret_value), "utf-8"), computed_url.encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest()
    query_parameters["signature"] = urlsafe_b64encode(signature).decode()
    return f"{base_url}?{urllib.parse.urlencode(query_parameters)}"
```

# Implementation Notes/Warnings

*Query Parameter Order*

It is extremely important that query parameters are applied in the specific order provided.  The signature is generated via a hash of the url, so it is imperative that both sides generate the string being fed into the hash exactly the same way.

*Link Generation Time*

It is naturally convenient to apply the redirect to TrueBiz with the signature at the time when the CRM page is generated.  However, due to the presence of the valid_until parameter, signed URLs may expire if the individual reading the page spends more than the maximum interval (5 minutes) before clicking the link to see the results in TrueBiz.  As such, we strongly recommend using a button and a click handler event to obtain the signed URL.

tags.name: Monitoring Integration Guide
tags.description:
# Business Purpose

Users of TrueBiz's Monitoring API want to monitor domains over time for issues, and be alerted when issues are found.

# Technical Overview

The monitoring api has three parts
- a management endpoint to start and stop monitoring domains
- a webhook endpoint to deliver alerts notifications to you
- an informational endpoint to retrieve machine-readable context about particular alerts

# Implementation Details

## Webhook Configuration

Prior to submitting any requests via the API, it is important to configure your webhooks. You can do this by logging
into TrueBiz's Web Portal at https://app.truebiz.io and clicking the 'Webhook Dashboard' button on the top right. This
will take you to the Dashboard for managing webhooks and you'll need to configure an endpoint to cover events
related to ad-hoc web presence reviews.

## API Key

To submit a request to TrueBiz, you will also need an API Key. If you do not already have one, contact your account
manager.


## Start monitoring a domain

To start monitoring a domain you will need to make a `HTTP` `POST` request to the `/api/v1/monitoring/start`
endpoint with the domain you with to register and your API key.

```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

response = httpx.post(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/start",
    json={
      "domain": "https://truebiz.io/",
    },
    headers=headers,
)
```


### Including an external identifier
If you wish to include an external identifier to tie back incoming alerts into your system, specify it alongside
the domain as `external_ref_id`.

```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

response = httpx.post(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/start",
    json={
      "domain": "https://truebiz.io/",
      "external_ref_id": "cus_NffrFeUfNV2Hib",
    },
    headers=headers,
)
```

This value will be included in the alert as `external_ref_id` for all alerts related to this domain.

If you wish to change the external identifier later, you will first need to stop monitoring (see below) 
and the restart monitoring with the new `external_ref_id`.

### Specifying a particular monitoring package
TrueBiz currently has two available monitoring packages: basic, and extended. Contact your account manager
to discuss the differences in the kinds of checks included and which is appropriate for your use case.

By default, TrueBiz will enable the basic monitoring package if you don't specify a package, but this can be
changed by including a `packages` entry in your request.

**Basic package**

```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

response = httpx.post(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/start",
    json={
      "domain": "https://truebiz.io/",
      "packages": [
        { "type": "io.truebiz.monitoring.packages.basic" }
      ]
    },
    headers=headers,
)
```

**Extended package**

```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

response = httpx.post(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/start",
    json={
      "domain": "https://truebiz.io/",
      "packages": [
        { "type": "io.truebiz.monitoring.packages.extended" }
      ]
    },
    headers=headers,
)
```

If you wish to change the package for this domain later, you will first need to stop monitoring (see below) 
and the restart monitoring with the new `packages` selection.

### Specifying a particular frequency
TrueBiz can perform monitoring checks more or less frequently depending on your needs. Currently there is a
weekly and a monthly option.

By default, TrueBiz will perform monitoring checks monthly if you don't specify a frequency, but this can be
changed by including a `packages` entry with a frequency in your request. Note that you will need to specify
both the package type as well as the frequency (see above for a discussion about available package types).

**Weekly frequency**

```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

response = httpx.post(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/start",
    json={
      "domain": "https://truebiz.io/",
      "packages": [
        { 
            "type": "io.truebiz.monitoring.packages.basic",
            "frequency": {
                "days": 7,
            }
        }
      ]
    },
    headers=headers,
)
```

**Monthly frequency**

```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

response = httpx.post(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/start",
    json={
      "domain": "https://truebiz.io/",
      "packages": [
        { 
            "type": "io.truebiz.monitoring.packages.basic",
            "frequency": {
                "days": 30,
            }
        }
      ]
    },
    headers=headers,
)
```

If you wish to change the check frequency for this domain later, you will first need to stop monitoring (see below) 
and the restart monitoring with the new `packages` and frequency selection.

## Stop monitoring a domain

To stop monitoring a domain you will need to make a `HTTP` `POST` request to the `/api/v1/monitoring/stop`
endpoint with the domain you with to stop and your API key.

If you wish to make changes to the way TrueBiz monitors a domain, you will first need to stop monitoring it,
and the start monitoring it (see above) with the new configuration.

Note that this will not delete any historical data or alerts, merely prevent future checks from running.
Any checks that are already running will continue to run to completion.

```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

response = httpx.post(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/stop",
    json={
      "domain": "https://truebiz.io/",
    },
    headers=headers,
)
```

If successful, the response returned will be the configuration last used for monitoring the domain. 
(This response can be useful when making configuration changes).

If a domain is not currently being monitored, this endpoint will return an error.

## List all monitored domains

To see what domains TrueBiz is currently monitoring, make a `HTTP` `GET` request to the
`/api/v1/monitoring/domains` endpoint with your API key.

```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

response = httpx.get(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/domains",
    headers=headers,
)
```

The response is paginated and will list all domains that TrueBiz is monitoring for your account.

### Filtering and sorting
The endpoint supports several filtering and sorting options

- `domain`
- `external_ref_id`
- `package_type`

#### Filtering by `domain`

```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

response = httpx.get(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/domains?domain=truebiz.io",
    headers=headers,
)
```

#### Sorting by `domain`

```python
import httpx

# ascending
response = httpx.get(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/domains?order_by=domain",
    headers=headers,
)

# descending
response = httpx.get(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/domains?order_by=-domain",
    headers=headers,
```


#### Filtering by `package_type`

```python
# descending

    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/domains?order_by=-package_type",
    headers=headers,

```

## Receiving and processing webhook events
After configuring your webhook endpoint to receive TrueBiz monitoring alerts (see above), TrueBiz
will begin sending webhook events to your endpoint for every new monitoring alert.

Monitoring alert webhook messages have the following basic shape:

```json
{
    "type": "io.truebiz.monitoring.alert",
    "created_at": "2025-01-12T08:15:42.555073+00:00",
    "alert_detail_link": {
        "href": "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/alerts/94347f66-0601-4b94-adca-adea9d4daa82/",
    },
    "ui_portal_link": {
        "href": "https://app.truebiz.io/monitoring/alerts/94347f66-0601-4b94-adca-adea9d4daa82/",
    }
}
```

**It is important to always verify the signature and hashes of any webhook messages you receive.**
For more information see https://docs.svix.com/receiving/verifying-payloads/how.

The `alert_detail_link` is a way to access machine-readable information (including any associated
external ids) about the via the TueBiz API (see below for detailed usage about the alert information API).

The `ui_portal_link` is a deep link to the TrueBiz portal, that provides the richest possible context
and human readable information about the alert.

## Retrieving machine-readable information about individual monitoring alerts
Information about individual alerts can be retrieved my making a `HTTP` `GET` request to the
`/api/v1/monitoring/alerts/<ALERT-ID>` endpoint with the alert id, and your API key. In the example below
`94347f66-0601-4b94-adca-adea9d4daa82` is the alert id.

```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

response = httpx.get(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/alerts/94347f66-0601-4b94-adca-adea9d4daa82",
    headers=headers,
)
```


## Retrieving machine-readable information about multiple monitoring alerts
The monitoring api also provides a list endpoint for all alerts in the system. The can be
accessed by making a `HTTP` `GET` request to the `/api/v1/monitoring/alerts/` with your API key.


```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

response = httpx.get(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/alerts/",
    headers=headers,
)
```

The response is paginated and will list all monitoring alerts that TrueBiz has issued to your account.

### Filtering and sorting
The endpoint supports several filtering and sorting options which can all be combined.

- `created_before`
- `created_after`
- `domain`
- `external_ref_id`
- `flagged_categories`

#### Filtering by creation date

```python
import httpx

headers = {"X-API-KEY": "<YOUR-API-KEY>"}

# before a certain date
response = httpx.get(
    "https://ae.truebiz.io/api/v1/monitoring/alerts/?created_before=2025-01-12T08:15:42.555073+00:00",
    headers=headers,

    headers=headers,
```
